title: R15b: gate/merge/executor integration — stale.py evidence in the gate, merged_at and changed_files stamped by merge(), gate stamps cleared on fix-round replies, allocation and active Jev routing hooks in executor.start, scout reuse check in spawn_scout
spec:
Why: merged pure modules need their call sites: daemon.stale_check/_record_stale_check (orchestrator/daemon.py:1050-1097) only knows path signals; merge.merge (orchestrator/merge.py:25-99) stamps no merged_at (merge wait undefined for Planner merges, AP P0 gap) and no changed_files (stale.overlapping_merge floor); executor.post_tool_result with replace_result=True (executor.py:215-247) leaves pipeline.gated_at set so gate() skips a task fixed by codex_reply (Planner had to clear it by hand on T-0570/T-0574 today); executor.start (executor.py:249-300) picks executors without allocation or active Jev adjustment; mcp.spawn_scout (mcp.py:75-77) launches without the scout_evidence reuse check.
What. Tests: this repo runs unittest; every acceptance test id is a `def test_name(self)` method inside a unittest.TestCase subclass in the named file; no pytest fixtures; use the daemon test harness in tests/_harness.py.
1. Stale: daemon.stale_check(task) delegates to stale.evidence(task, graph_links=stale.load_links(), graph=interference.load_graph(), tasks=bus.read(role='execute')) and returns its dict (today's keys base, goal_head, moved_count, stale_paths, risk remain; signals/risk_reasons/graph added); _record_stale_check writes stale.row(...) with action recorded; _stale_rebase writes rows with action rebased/rebase_conflict; risk 'medium' is treated like 'low' for the stale_rebase decision (only high rebases).
2. merge.merge: on status merged, bus.update also sets merged_at=time.time() (top-level, mirrored into pipeline.merged_at when absent) and changed_files = git diff --name-only previous_sha..sha (bounded to 500 paths). scorecard.parallelism merge_wait_s must read either location (read stamp helper accepts pipeline or top-level; already does per _stamp — verify with a test).
3. executor.post_tool_result(replace_result=True): pop pipeline keys gated_at, gated_at_lease, gated_at_done and hold_reason/resume_hint gate residue, so gate() re-runs on the new head; record pipeline.regated_by='codex_reply'.
4. executor.start: after scores = scorecard.scores(...), if [jev.routing].mode == active: routing = jev_route.shadow_context(t, pool) and scores = jev_route.active_scores(t, pool, routing['eligible'], routing['classification'], routing['evidence'], scores); then if [allocation].mode != off: ev = allocation.evidence_for([e.id for e in eligible], scorecard.task_class(t)); choice = allocation.choose(t, eligible ids, baseline=pool.pick_executor(...).id, priority=critical_path.explain(t id, tasks), ready_priorities=..., evidence=ev); allocation.record(t id, choice); in active mode ex = pool.executors[choice['executor']]; shadow leaves the baseline. Any exception in these hooks -> baseline pick, error logged in the run row.
5. mcp.spawn_scout(task_id): before _bg, check = scout_evidence.reuse_check(task spec, objective=constraints.objective, head_sha=HEAD); scout_evidence.record_decision(...); when check['sufficient'] and constraints.force is not true, return {'task': id, 'status': 'skipped: reusable evidence', 'hits': check['hits']} and post the task result as done with the hits as findings (provenance repo, summary naming the reused ids); otherwise spawn as today.
Safety: security review path and reviews_expected untouched; allocation never returns an ineligible executor; all hooks fail open to today's behaviour.
acceptance: tests/test_daemon.py::test_stale_check_returns_extended_evidence_and_only_high_rebases — stale_check output has signals and risk_reasons; a medium risk never triggers _stale_rebase
tests/test_merge.py::test_merge_stamps_merged_at_and_changed_files — a successful merge leaves merged_at and a changed_files list on the task
tests/test_executor.py::test_reply_result_clears_gate_stamps_for_regating — post_tool_result with replace_result removes gated_at keys and sets regated_by

tests/test_executor.py::test_start_uses_allocation_only_in_active_mode_and_fails_open — shadow mode keeps the baseline executor and writes an allocation decision row; active mode uses the chosen eligible executor; a raising allocation.choose falls back to baseline

tests/test_executor.py::test_start_applies_active_jev_scores_only_when_mode_active — with [jev.routing].mode active the scores passed to pick_executor are the adjusted ones; in shadow they are unchanged
tests/test_mcp.py::test_spawn_scout_skips_when_reusable_evidence_is_sufficient — sufficient fresh evidence returns skipped with hits and posts the scout result; force true spawns anyway

constraints.interface_contract: stale_check(task) keeps today's keys and adds signals, risk_reasons, graph; merge() stamps merged_at and changed_files; post_tool_result(replace_result=True) clears gated_at*; executor.start hooks read [allocation].mode and [jev.routing].mode; spawn_scout returns status 'skipped: reusable evidence' when sufficient

result.summary: superseded by R15b v2 after spec review T-0655 (executor.start builds the ready set and critical-path priorities itself from the bus; two-task allocation test)

events.hold_reason: planner: serialized behind T-0646 (both edit daemon.py); release when R15a merges

spec_review_risks.issue: The allocation hook in executor.start needs `priority=critical_path.explain(task_id, tasks)` and `ready_priorities` (other ready tasks' critical-path priorities) to pick the critical vs non-critical factor in allocation.choose. But executor.start (called from mcp.codex/codex_reply and from daemon._dispatch_worker) only ever has the single task_id in scope — the `tasks` dependency-graph dict and per-tick `ready_priorities` are built in daemon.dispatch() (via _wave_tasks/candidate_ids, daemon.py:701-743) and never threaded through spawn_async(_dispatch_worker,...) or into executor.start's signature. The spec's '...' for ready_priorities leaves this undefined, so an implementer can satisfy the acceptance test with a degenerate single-task ready_priorities list (e.g. just [priority['critical_path_s']]), which makes `current_path >= max(ready_priorities)` trivially true and always selects settings['critical_factor'] — silently defeating T-0634's non-critical discount without failing any test.

test_start_uses_allocation_only_in_active_mode_and_fails_open, as scoped, does not require ready_priorities to reflect any task besides the one under dispatch, so it cannot catch the degenerate single-task implementation described above.
